facts.label: Marriage license fee
facts.quote: The fee for a Marriage License is $35.

facts.label: Civil ceremony at the City Clerk's office (any borough)
facts.quote: The cost is $25, payable by credit/debit card or money order.

facts.label: Waiting period
facts.display: 24 hours after you receive the license
facts.quote: The marriage ceremony needs to take place at least 24 hours after you receive the License.

facts.label: How long the license is valid
facts.display: Usually 60 days (180 days for active military)
facts.quote: Marriage Licenses are usually valid for 60 days. For active military personnel, the License is valid for 180 days.

facts.label: ID you bring
facts.display: The same type of photo ID you used for the license: you, your spouse and a witness
facts.quote: You, your prospective spouse, and at least one witness must bring the same type of photo identification that was used to obtain the Marriage License.

facts.label: How to get the license / book the ceremony
facts.display: Appointment only, online (Project Cupid, nyc.gov/cupid) or by phone; no walk-ins
facts.quote: City Clerk offices do not provide walk-in services. You must make an appointment online or by phone.

facts.label: Where: you can apply at any borough office
facts.display: Appointment at any of the five borough City Clerk offices
facts.quote: A Marriage License is required to get married in New York State. You can make an appointment to apply at any borough office.

facts.label: Ceremonies are held in all five borough offices
facts.display: All five borough offices
facts.quote: The Office of the City Clerk performs marriage ceremonies throughout the day in all five City Clerk borough offices.

facts.label: Accepted ID for the license application
facts.display: Driver's license, non-driver ID, NYS learner's permit, IDNYC, US military ID, passport from any country (must be valid)
facts.quote: Identification Documents that are accepted: Driver's license (from the United States or one of its territories) Non driver's identification card (from the United States or one of its territories) Learner's permit from New York State only IDNYC United States Military Identification Card A valid passport from any country

facts.label: Expired ID
facts.display: Expired documents are not accepted
facts.quote: All documents must be valid. Expired documents will not be accepted.

facts.label: Minimum age
facts.display: 18 and older
facts.quote: You must be 18 and older to be permitted to marry in New York State.

facts.label: License the same day
facts.display: You leave with the license the same day if your documents are complete
facts.quote: If you provide all necessary documents, you will get a Marriage License on the same day.

facts.label: How to pay the license fee
facts.display: Credit or debit card, or money order payable to the City Clerk
facts.quote: You can pay by credit card (Visa, MasterCard, Discover, American Express), debit card (Visa or MasterCard) or a money order payable to the City Clerk.

facts.label: Witness
facts.display: At least one witness over 18
facts.quote: At least one witness over the age of 18

facts.label: Ceremony arrival hours
facts.display: Arrive between 8:30 AM and 3:15 PM, Monday to Friday
facts.quote: You, your prospective spouse, and witness should arrive between 8:30 AM and 3:15 PM, Monday through Friday.

facts.label: Ceremony group size
facts.display: No more than 6 attendees including the couple and the witness
facts.quote: There can be no more than 6 attendees, including you, your prospective spouse and the witness.

facts.label: Marriage certificate after a City Clerk ceremony
facts.display: Same day
facts.quote: Once the civil marriage ceremony is complete, you will get a Marriage Certificate on that same day.

facts.quote: You can request a Judicial Waiver from the County Clerk in the borough where you obtained your Marriage License. There is no fee.

steps: Book your appointment: City Clerk offices take no walk-ins, so you make an appointment online through Project Cupid (nyc.gov/cupid) or by phone.
Both of you go to a City Clerk borough office with valid photo ID and the $35 fee (card or money order); with complete documents you get the license the same day.
Wait at least 24 hours after you receive the license before the ceremony (a judge's waiver is possible, no fee). The license is usually valid for 60 days.
Book the City Clerk ceremony ($25) at any of the five borough offices and arrive between 8:30 AM and 3:15 PM, Monday to Friday.
Bring the license, at least one witness over 18 and the same type of photo ID used for the license; no more than 6 attendees in all.
After the ceremony you receive your Marriage Certificate the same day.
left_out: Certified copy fee for a marriage certificate: not stated on the NYC311 license or ceremony pages that were read.

Project Cupid appointment availability, lead times and any online booking fee: the Project Cupid booking system and cityclerk.nyc.gov pages are rendered by JavaScript, so nothing could be downloaded or quoted from them.

notes: Courthouse: cityclerk.nyc.gov pages are a JavaScript shell (every URL returns the same banner page), so all courthouse quotes come from the City's own NYC311 pages on portal.311.nyc.gov (an nyc.gov site that states 'The Official Website of the City of New York'). They agree with the City Clerk banner text (appointments only, no walk-ins, Project Cupid). Venues: 8 listed, one per venue, sorted by amount. Several do not print a guest count next to the price, so a second verified quote is attached (guests_evidence / weekend_evidence / requirements_evidence / elopement_evidence; verify_quotes.py checks those too). STATEN ISLAND HAS NO VENUE IN THE LIST. The only Staten Island lead with a printed number is Alice Austen House (aliceausten.org/rentals): it prints 'Rental fees are $500/hr' for outdoor wedding-ceremony rentals but no guest limit and no package, so it was dropped under the brief's rules. Snug Harbor, Historic Richmond Town, Staten Island Botanical Garden pages print no price; Venues on the Terrace showed its $1,495 Standard Package (80 people max, Eventective listing) only on an aggregator and its own site did not load. The web-search budget ran out before more Staten Island venues could be checked. Queens has one venue (Queens Party Hall's Occasions Hall); Queens Botanical Garden and Skylight Hall print no price on their own pages. Weak fits the coordinator may drop: Brooklyn Bridge Park is a public-park ceremony permit (up to 100 guests, no reception) and not a booked venue (its page says it is for a wedding ceremony, elopement, vow renewal); Queens Party Hall's Occasions Hall is a DIY 80-guest hall with a Mon-Thu base rate (its page heading says intimate and small wedding venues), not a wedding package; the Church of the Transfiguration fee schedule is titled 2024 and Episcopal rules apply. Wave Hill: the price_display is composed from two printed fees and amount 2000 is their sum ($500 rental fee + $1,500 required Partner Membership); the rental fee alone is $500. The same page prints an intimate event for up to 25 guests (Glyndor Terrace or Aquatic Garden, up to two hours, Tue/Wed/Fri 2-5 PM) at a $1,500 Partner Membership plus a $1,500 rental fee, and weekday ceremony-only (Pergola, up to 125 guests, 6-7:30 PM) at a $2,500 membership plus a $3,500 site fee. The Benjamin: micro-wedding packages are weekends only, 3 months' advance booking; The Romantic (couple and officiant) is $1,000 and The Royal (20 guests or less) is $3,000 plus tax and service charge. Not usable: Central Park Conservancy's Conservatory Garden permit page prints no fee; Atrium82, Brooklyn Winery and Hotel Giraffe print no small-wedding price on their own pages; Royal Blueprint (Brooklyn), Deity Events and Loft of EP own sites did not load. Photographer: Erica Morris's site is a Google Site (text is in the curl HTML). Her City Hall Package 2 is ceremony (30 minutes or under) plus a 30-minute shoot, so about 1 hour; hours=1 is that reading. Florist: NYC Flower Pop is a Google Site; the $150 bouquet is a pickup price (a courier within Manhattan is +$40, boutonniere $25).
